proof_skeleton_nl: First recode Kunz coordinates by the homogeneous Apéry transformation w_i = m x_i + i. Then apply a hard Hilbert-series positivity statement asserting that the counting generating series F_m(t)=sum_h |K_{m,h}| t^h has nonnegative first-difference series. A formal coefficient-extraction lemma converts that identity into |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}| for every g. Since the two sets are finite, a standard finite-set lemma then yields an injective map between them.

steps.derives: For the fixed integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, both K_{m,g} and K_{m,g+1} are finite sets: apply L1 once with the parameter g and once with the parameter g+1. Therefore their cardinalities are ordinary natural numbers and can later be compared and used in a finite-set injection argument.

By the change of variables w_i = m x_i + i from L2, every slice K_{m,h} is bijective to a congruence-restricted slice of one fixed homogeneous system of inequalities. In particular, the family h |-> |K_{m,h}| is naturally a graded counting function coming from a single homogenized cone model.

Let H_m(h)=|K_{m,h}| for h >= 0 and let F_m(t)=sum_{h>=0} H_m(h)t^h. Applying L3 for the fixed value of m gives a formal power series G_m(t)=sum_{h>=0} c_h t^h with each c_h >= 0 such that (1-t)F_m(t)=H_m(0)+tG_m(t).

Apply L4 to the formal power series F_m(t) and C(t)=G_m(t) from A3. This yields H_m(h+1)-H_m(h)=c_h for every integer h >= 0. Since each c_h is nonnegative, one concludes that H_m(h) <= H_m(h+1) for every h >= 0; equivalently, |K_{m,h}| <= |K_{m,h+1}| for every h >= 0.

Specializing the inequality from A4 to h=g gives |K_{m,g}| <= |K_{m,g+1}|. Together with the finiteness of K_{m,g} and K_{m,g+1} from A1, L5 applies with A=K_{m,g} and B=K_{m,g+1}. Therefore there exists an injective function f:K_{m,g} -> K_{m,g+1}.

Set J_{m,g}=f. Therefore, for the given integers m >= 2 and g >= 0, if K_{m,g} denotes the set of all tuples x=(x_1,...,x_{m-1}) of positive integers such that x_1+...+x_{m-1}=g and for all i,j in {1,...,m-1} one has x_i+x_j >= x_{i+j} when i+j < m and x_i+x_j+1 >= x_{i+j-m} when i+j > m, and K_{m,g+1} is defined analogously with coordinate sum g+1, then there exists an injective function J_{m,g} from K_{m,g} to K_{m,g+1}.
steps.trivial_justification: This is just a renaming of the injective function f obtained in A5.
